questions.questionText: Mass and weight differ because:

questions.explanation: Constant velocity = zero acceleration = balanced forces.

questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 100/10 = 10 m/s.

questions.explanation: X-axis = independent variable. Y-axis = dependent variable.

questions.questionText: A well-designed data table includes:
questions.explanation: Tables = clear headings + units + organized data.

questions.questionText: In human experiments, ethical principle requires:
questions.explanation: Ethical research = informed consent + safety + minimal harm.

questions.questionText: An open-ended question:
questions.explanation: Open-ended = variety of answers. Closed-ended = fixed/limited.

questions.questionText: A scientific model is used to:

options.label: A
options.text: Represent and explain a system or concept

questions.explanation: Model = simplified representation of system/concept.

questions.questionText: The cell cycle consists of:

options.label: A
options.text: Interphase (G1, S, G2) and M phase (mitosis)

questions.explanation: Cell cycle = interphase (growth, DNA replication) + M phase (division).

questions.questionText: Stem cells are unique because they can:

options.label: A
options.text: Develop into many different cell types

questions.explanation: Stem cells = undifferentiated cells that can specialize.

questions.questionText: Active transport differs from passive transport because active transport:
questions.explanation: Active = ATP needed. Passive = no energy needed.

questions.questionText: Endocytosis is the process of:

options.label: B
options.text: Releasing materials OUT of the cell

questions.explanation: Endocytosis = cell takes in materials via membrane infolding.

questions.questionText: Chlorophyll captures light energy for:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll = pigment that traps light for photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: Plasmolysis occurs when plant cells lose water and the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall. This happens in:
questions.explanation: Hypertonic = water exits cell by osmosis = plasmolysis.

questions.questionText: Cell sap is found in the:
questions.explanation: Vacuole contains cell sap (water + sugars + salts).

questions.questionText: Yeast cells are classified as:
questions.explanation: Yeast = eukaryotic fungus with membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.questionText: Which organelle is in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplast = plant only (for photosynthesis).

questions.questionText: Protein folding and modification occur in the:
questions.explanation: ER + Golgi = protein processing and packaging.

questions.questionText: DNA in a eukaryotic cell is located in the:
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic DNA = mostly in nucleus. Some in mitochondria/chloroplast.

questions.questionText: The cell membrane is composed mainly of:
questions.explanation: Cell membrane = phospholipid bilayer + proteins (fluid mosaic).

questions.questionText: RDA stands for:
questions.explanation: RDA = Recommended Dietary Allowance = daily nutrient intake.

questions.questionText: Macronutrients include:
questions.explanation: Macronutrients = carbs + proteins + fats (needed in large amounts).

questions.questionText: Micronutrients include:
questions.explanation: Micronutrients = vitamins + minerals (needed in small amounts).

questions.questionText: Glucose is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Glucose = simple sugar (monosaccharide).

questions.questionText: Which is a good source of polyunsaturated fats?
questions.explanation: Plant oils = polyunsaturated. Butter/lard = saturated fats.

questions.questionText: A complete protein source contains:
questions.explanation: Complete protein = all essential amino acids (e.g., eggs, meat, soy).

questions.questionText: An average adult typically needs about how many calories per day?
questions.explanation: Average adult = ~2000 kcal/day (varies).

questions.questionText: Athletes generally need MORE:
questions.explanation: Athletes need more energy (carbs) and protein for performance.

questions.questionText: Pregnant women need EXTRA:
questions.explanation: Pregnancy = extra folate, iron, Ca, protein for fetus development.

questions.questionText: Anorexia nervosa is:
questions.explanation: Anorexia = eating disorder with severe food restriction + low body weight.

questions.questionText: Freezing food preserves it by:
questions.explanation: Freezing low temp slows/inhibits microbial growth & enzyme activity.

questions.questionText: Generally, which type of compound is most soluble in water?
questions.explanation: Ionic/polar compounds dissolve well in polar water ('like dissolves like').

questions.questionText: Recrystallization is best used to:
questions.explanation: Recrystallization = dissolve + selective crystallization to purify.

questions.questionText: Solvent extraction is used to:
questions.explanation: Extraction = solute moves between two immiscible solvents.

questions.questionText: Sublimation is the change from:

options.label: A
options.text: Solid directly to gas (without liquid phase)

questions.explanation: Sublimation = solid → gas (skipping liquid). E.g., dry ice, naphthalene.

questions.questionText: Decantation is best used to:

options.label: A
options.text: Pour off liquid from a settled solid (without disturbing)

questions.explanation: Decanting = carefully pour liquid leaving sediment behind.

questions.questionText: Filtration at a water treatment plant removes:
questions.explanation: Filtration = removes undissolved solids. Dissolved need other methods.

questions.questionText: A centrifuge separates mixtures based on:
questions.explanation: Centrifuge = spin fast = dense particles move to bottom by density difference.

questions.questionText: Reverse osmosis is used to:
questions.explanation: Reverse osmosis = pressure forces water through membrane = removes ions.

questions.questionText: Diffusion rate increases with:
questions.explanation: Higher T = more KE = faster diffusion. Smaller particles diffuse faster.

questions.questionText: Brownian motion is the:

options.label: A
options.text: Random zigzag motion of small particles in fluid

options.label: B
options.text: Upward motion of hot air only

questions.explanation: Brownian motion = random movement due to collisions with molecules.

questions.questionText: Hexane (non-polar) and water do NOT mix because:

options.label: A
options.text: Polar water and non-polar hexane are immiscible

questions.explanation: 'Like dissolves like' = polar mixes with polar only. Non-polar doesn't mix.

questions.questionText: From a solubility curve, at 50°C the solubility of KNO₃ is found by:

options.label: A
options.text: Drawing a line from 50°C up to the curve, then across to read solubility

questions.explanation: Reading a solubility curve = draw lines from values to axes.

questions.questionText: A strong acid has:

options.label: A
options.text: More free H⁺ ions in solution (complete ionization)

questions.explanation: Strong acid = fully ionized in water = high [H⁺].

questions.questionText: A chemical bottle with an 'irritant' symbol means:

options.label: A
options.text: Can cause irritation to skin/eyes/respiratory system

questions.explanation: Irritant pictogram = warning for irritation hazards.

questions.questionText: Lemon juice and vinegar are examples of:
questions.explanation: Lemon juice, vinegar = common weak acids.

questions.questionText: If 0.5 mol HCl reacts with NaOH (1:1 ratio), how many mol NaOH needed?
questions.explanation: 1:1 ratio = same moles. So 0.5 mol NaOH needed.

questions.questionText: CO₂ exhaled by humans makes blood slightly more:
questions.explanation: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ (carbonic acid) = slightly acidic blood.

questions.questionText: Reactivity of acid with magnesium increases with:
questions.explanation: Reaction rate ↑ with concentration ↑ and temperature ↑.

questions.questionText: To test a colorless solution suspected to be acidic, the best indicator is:
questions.explanation: Universal indicator covers full pH range = best for unknown.

questions.questionText: Universal indicator is made by:
questions.explanation: Universal = mixture of several indicators gives full pH range color change.

questions.questionText: Natural litmus indicator is extracted from:
questions.explanation: Litmus comes from lichens (small plant-like organisms).

questions.questionText: Acid + metal oxide produces:
questions.explanation: Acid + metal oxide → salt + water (no gas here).

questions.questionText: A rocket launching uses which laws?

options.label: A
options.text: Newton's 3rd law (action-reaction, expelled gas pushes rocket up)

questions.explanation: Rocket propulsion = Newton's 3rd law (every action has reaction).

questions.questionText: An object in water feels 'lighter' because of:
questions.explanation: Buoyancy = water pushes up = apparent weight = real - buoyancy.

questions.questionText: An object weighs 20 N in air and 12 N in water. Buoyancy force =
questions.explanation: Buoyancy = apparent weight loss = 20 - 12 = 8 N.

questions.questionText: An inclined plane helps by:

options.label: A
options.text: Reducing the force needed by spreading over distance

questions.explanation: Inclined plane reduces force needed by increasing distance (work conserved).

questions.questionText: A single fixed pulley provides:
questions.explanation: Fixed pulley = MA = 1 (only changes direction, not force magnitude).

questions.questionText: A longer lever arm provides:
questions.explanation: Lever MA = (effort arm / load arm). Longer effort = less force.

questions.questionText: Force 10 N moves an object 5 m. Work done =
A 3 kg object at 4 m height (g=10). GPE =
When a gun fires, the bullet moves forward and the gun:
questions.explanation: Gun kicks backward due to conservation of momentum (Newton 3rd).

questions.questionText: An ELASTIC collision differs from INELASTIC because elastic:
questions.explanation: Elastic: KE conserved. Inelastic: KE lost to heat/deformation.

questions.questionText: Diffraction occurs when light:

options.label: A
options.text: Passes through a small opening or around an edge

questions.explanation: Diffraction = bending of light at edges/around obstacles.

questions.questionText: Young's double slit experiment demonstrates:
questions.explanation: Double slit produces interference pattern = light has wave nature.

questions.questionText: Lens maker's formula relates focal length to:

options.label: A
options.text: Refractive indices and radii of curvature

questions.explanation: Lens maker = 1/f = (n-1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂).

questions.questionText: Power of a lens (in diopters) equals:
questions.explanation: P = 1/f (diopters, with f in meters).

questions.questionText: A mirage is NOT regular reflection because:

options.label: A
options.text: It involves refraction in air layers (not from a surface)

questions.explanation: Mirage = refraction through hot air layers near ground.

questions.questionText: Fiber optic cables transmit data using:

options.label: A
options.text: Total internal reflection of light inside glass

questions.explanation: Fiber optic = light trapped by TIR inside glass = data transmission.

questions.questionText: A hologram records:
questions.explanation: Hologram = interference pattern records 3D info (intensity + phase).

questions.questionText: Cone cells in the eye are responsible for:
questions.explanation: Cones = color vision (bright light). Rods = dim light (B&W).

questions.questionText: Color blindness is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Color blindness = genetic defect in cone photoreceptors.

questions.questionText: A coin at the bottom of a pool appears:
questions.explanation: Refraction at water surface makes objects appear shallower.

questions.questionText: Looking at a fish in a pond, its image appears:
questions.explanation: Refraction makes underwater objects appear shallower than real.

questions.questionText: A black body is a perfect:
questions.explanation: Black body = absorbs all radiation + emits maximally at each wavelength.

questions.questionText: Diffusion of gases occurs FASTER at:
questions.explanation: Higher T = more KE = faster diffusion.

questions.questionText: Efficiency of a heat engine =
questions.explanation: Efficiency = W_out / Q_in × 100%.

questions.questionText: Carnot cycle represents:
questions.explanation: Carnot = theoretical ideal reversible engine = max possible efficiency.

questions.questionText: Among common metals, the BEST heat conductor is:
questions.explanation: Thermal conductivity: silver > copper > aluminum > steel > lead.

questions.questionText: A heat sink in electronics works by:

options.label: A
options.text: Conducting heat away from components (large surface area)

questions.explanation: Heat sink = large surface area + high conductivity = dissipates heat.

questions.questionText: In a thermostat, a bimetallic strip bends when heated because:

options.label: A
options.text: Two metals expand at different rates

questions.explanation: Bimetallic = two metals with different expansion rates = bends with temperature.

questions.questionText: Compared to metals, water's specific heat is:
questions.explanation: Water SHC = ~4200 J/kg°C, much higher than metals (e.g., iron ~450).

questions.questionText: A home radiator transfers heat to room mostly by:

options.label: A
options.text: Convection (and radiation) - air heats and rises

questions.explanation: Radiator heats air = convection current circulates heat.

questions.questionText: Bimetallic strips are also used in:

options.label: A
options.text: Oven temperature controls and circuit breakers

questions.explanation: Bimetallic = thermostats + circuit breakers + fire alarms.

questions.questionText: Bridges and concrete buildings have expansion joints to:
questions.explanation: Expansion joints accommodate thermal expansion = prevent cracking.

questions.questionText: If 3 identical resistors are connected in series, total resistance is:
questions.explanation: Series: R_total = R1 + R2 + R3 = 3R.

questions.questionText: Kirchhoff's current law states that at a junction:

options.label: A
options.text: Sum of currents in = sum of currents out

questions.explanation: KCL: ΣI_in = ΣI_out (charge conservation at junction).

questions.questionText: Kirchhoff's voltage law states that around a closed loop:

options.label: A
options.text: Sum of EMFs = sum of voltage drops

questions.explanation: KVL: ΣEMF = Σ(IR) (energy conservation around loop).

questions.questionText: Pure silicon is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Silicon = semiconductor (conductivity between metal and insulator).

questions.questionText: A P-N junction allows current to flow mainly:
questions.explanation: Diode = allows current in one direction (forward bias).

questions.questionText: An LDR (light dependent resistor) resistance:
questions.explanation: LDR = more light = lower resistance.

questions.questionText: An LED (Light Emitting Diode):
questions.explanation: LED = emits light when current flows in forward direction.

questions.questionText: Transistors typically have:
questions.explanation: Transistor = 3 terminals (base, collector, emitter).

questions.questionText: A capacitor in a circuit stores:
questions.explanation: Capacitor stores charge (and electric field energy).

questions.questionText: An inductor resists changes in:
questions.explanation: Inductor = opposes change in current (by generating back-EMF).

questions.questionText: In a running motor, the induced EMF opposes the applied EMF - this is:
questions.explanation: Back EMF = induced EMF opposite to applied EMF (motor efficiency mechanism).

questions.questionText: An electric generator converts:
questions.explanation: Generator = mechanical rotation (via electromagnetic induction) → electricity.

questions.questionText: A simple AC generator produces EMF by:

options.label: A
options.text: Rotating a coil in a magnetic field

questions.explanation: AC generator = rotating coil in magnetic field = induced AC EMF.
